chapterNote: A psalm for when injustice has a throne. It opens by asking the God of vengeance — the requiting He reserved for Himself and forbade to us — to shine forth and rise as Judge of the earth. The wicked are exulting, gushing insolence, crushing His people, murdering the widow, the sojourner, and the orphan — all the while saying, 'Yah does not see.' The middle of the psalm answers that creed with the plainest argument in the Psalter: He who planted the ear, does He not hear? He who formed the eye, does He not see? He who disciplines the nations and taught man to think knows exactly what men are thinking, and rates it a breath. Then it turns personal. Blessed is the man God disciplines and teaches from His law; the LORD will not abandon His inheritance; if the LORD had not been my help my soul would have settled in silence; when I said my foot is slipping, Your covenant love propped me up; when my anxious thoughts multiplied, Your consolations delighted my soul. The sharpest line is political: a throne that manufactures misery by statute has no alliance with God. He is a rock, not a treaty partner, and the wicked will be handed back their own work.

1.text: God of vengeance, O LORD — God of vengeance, blaze out in light!
1.amp: O LORD [YHWH] God [El], to whom vengeance [neqamah] belongs ['God of revenges', El neqamah, the KJV margin]; O God [El], to whom vengeance [neqamah] belongs, show ['shine forth', yapha, the KJV margin] Yourself.
1.notes: El-neqamot YHWH El neqamot hophia (H410, H5360, H3068, H3313): 'God of vengeances', the margin's literal, twice — neqamah, the requiting that belongs to God alone (Deuteronomy 32:35, which Paul quotes to forbid it to us, Romans 12:19) — SHINE FORTH, the margin's verb, Psalm 50:2's theophany. The prayer asks God to do the one thing He reserved for Himself.

2.text: Rise up, Judge of the earth; pay back to the proud what they have earned.
2.amp: Lift up [nasa] Yourself, You judge [shaphat] of the earth [eretz]: render [shub — return] a reward [gemul — recompense] to the proud [geah].
2.notes: hinnase shophet ha-arets (H5375, H8199, H776): LIFT Yourself up, Judge of the earth — Abraham's title for Him (Genesis 18:25); hasheb gemul al-geim (H7725, H1576, H1343): RETURN recompense on the proud — Psalm 28:4's exact request. The psalm wants nothing more than the accurate.

3.text: How long will the wicked, O LORD — how long will the wicked celebrate?
3.amp: LORD [YHWH], how long shall the wicked [rasha], how long shall the wicked [rasha] triumph [alaz — exult]?
3.notes: ad-matai reshaim YHWH ad-matai reshaim yaalozu (H7563, H3068, H5937): how long, wicked — LORD — how long will the wicked EXULT? The doubled question is the lament's oldest form (Psalm 13:1-2; Habakkuk 1:2; Revelation 6:10); alaz is the joy-verb of Psalm 28:7, here in the wrong mouths.

4.text: They pour out words, they speak insolence; all the workers of iniquity brag about themselves.
4.amp: How long shall they utter [naba — gush, pour forth] and speak [dabar] hard things? and all the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven] boast [amar] themselves?
4.notes: yabbiu yedabberu ataq (H5042, H1696): they GUSH — naba, the spring-verb of Psalm 19:2 — they speak ataq, the insolent 'hard thing' of Psalm 31:18; yitammeru kol-poale aven (H559, H6466, H205): all the workers of wickedness 'say themselves' — talk themselves up. The offence is verbal first; the violence comes in verse 6.

5.text: They crush Your people, O LORD, and they grind down Your inheritance.
5.amp: They break in pieces [daka — crush] Your people [am], O LORD [YHWH], and afflict [anah — humble, grind down] Your heritage [nachalah].
5.notes: ammekha YHWH yedakkeu (H5971, H3068, H1792): YOUR people they CRUSH — daka, Psalm 143:3's verb — ve-nachalatekha yeannu (H5159, H6031): and Your inheritance they grind down. The possessives are the argument: what is being crushed is God's own property (cf. Psalm 28:9).

6.text: They kill the widow and the sojourner, and they murder the fatherless;
6.amp: They slay [harag] the widow [almanah] and the stranger [ger — sojourner], and murder [ratsach] the fatherless [yatom].
6.notes: almanah ve-ger yaharogu vi-tomim yeratsechu (H490, H1616, H2026, H3490, H7523): widow, sojourner, orphan — the Torah's protected triad (Deuteronomy 10:18; 24:17) — killed, and MURDERED: ratsach, the sixth commandment's own verb (Exodus 20:13). The oppressors have gone straight to the people God said He personally defends.

7.text: and they say, 'Yah does not see; the God of Jacob pays no attention.'
7.amp: Yet they say [amar], The LORD [Yah] shall not see [raah], neither shall the God [Elohim] of Jacob [Yaaqob] regard [bin — discern] it.
7.notes: va-yomeru lo yireh-Yah (H559, H7200, H3050): and they say, 'Yah does not see' — the short Name, used as if it were a small god's — ve-lo-yabin Elohe Yaaqob (H995, H430, H3290): 'and the God of Jacob does not DISCERN'. Psalm 10:11 and 64:5's creed of the practical atheist, now the murderers' — and verses 8-11 answer it with the plainest argument in the Psalter.

8.text: Understand this, you dullest of the people; you fools, when will you get wise?
8.amp: Understand [bin], you brutish [baar — dull as cattle] among the people [am]: and you fools [kesil], when will you be wise [sakal]?
8.notes: binu boarim ba-am (H995, H1197, H5971): DISCERN, you brutish among the people — the same bin the wicked denied to God (v. 7), thrown back; u-khesilim matai taskilu (H3684, H7919): and fools, when will you be wise? — Psalm 49:10's kesil. The psalmist turns from praying about the wicked to lecturing them: the God-does-not-see position is not evil first; it is stupid.

9.text: Does the One who planted the ear fail to hear? Does the One who formed the eye fail to see?
9.amp: He that planted [nata] the ear [ozen], shall He not hear [shama]? He that formed [yatsar] the eye [ayin], shall He not see [nabat — look]?
9.notes: ha-nota ozen ha-lo yishma (H5193, H241, H8085): the PLANTER of the ear — the gardener's verb — does He not hear? im-yotser ayin ha-lo yabbit (H3335, H5869, H5027): the FORMER of the eye — the potter's verb, Genesis 2:7's — does He not look? The argument from design run backward: whatever made the instruments of perception can hardly lack the faculty. Verses 9-10 are the Psalter's clearest piece of natural theology.

10.text: He who disciplines the nations — will He not correct? He who teaches man knowledge —
10.amp: He that chastises [yasar — disciplines] the heathen [goy — nations], shall not He correct [yakach — reprove]? He that teaches [lamad] man [adam] knowledge [daat], shall not He know?
10.notes: ha-yoser goyim ha-lo yokhiach (H3256, H1471, H3198): the DISCIPLINER of nations — does He not reprove? ha-melammed adam daat (H3925, H120, H1847): the Teacher of man's knowledge — the sentence breaks off; the KJV supplies 'shall not he know' from verse 11. The One who runs history's school and taught the race to think is not Himself unaware.

11.text: The LORD knows what man plans, and knows it for nothing but vapor.
11.amp: The LORD [YHWH] knows [yada] the thoughts [machashabah — plans] of man [adam], that they are vanity [hebel — a breath].
11.notes: YHWH yodea machshebot adam ki-hemmah habel (H3068, H3045, H4284, H120, H1892): the LORD KNOWS the thoughts of adam — that they are hebel, Ecclesiastes' word, vapor. The answer to 'He does not see' (v. 7): He sees the thoughts behind the murders, and rates them. Paul quotes the line of the wise of this world (1 Corinthians 3:20), reading 'the wise' for 'man' — the Greek Psalter's text.

12.text: Blessed is the man You discipline, O Yah, and teach out of Your law,
12.amp: Blessed [esher — happy] is the man [geber] whom You chasten [yasar — discipline], O LORD [Yah], and teach [lamad] him out of Your law [torah];
12.notes: ashre ha-geber asher-teyasserennu Yah (H835, H1397, H3256, H3050): HAPPY the man You DISCIPLINE, Yah — the same yasar with which God schools the nations (v. 10), now a beatitude — u-mi-toratekha telammedennu (H8451, H3925): and teach him from Your torah. Job 5:17, Proverbs 3:11-12, and Hebrews 12:5-11 stand behind the verse: the chastened man is the loved one.

13.text: to give him quiet in the days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
13.amp: That You may give him rest [shaqat — quiet] from the days [yom] of adversity [ra], until the pit [shachat] be digged [karah] for the wicked [rasha].
13.notes: le-hashqit lo mi-yme ra (H8252, H3117, H7451): to make him QUIET from the days of evil — shaqat, the calm of a land at peace (Judges 3:11) — ad yikkareh la-rasha shachat (H3738, H7563, H7845): until the pit is dug for the wicked. Discipline as the thing that lets a man wait calmly while the shovel is still working (cf. Psalm 37:7).

14.text: For the LORD will not cast off His people, and He will not abandon His inheritance;
14.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] will not cast off [natash — leave] His people [am], neither will He forsake [azab] His inheritance [nachalah].
14.notes: ki lo-yittosh YHWH ammo ve-nachalato lo yaazob (H3068, H5203, H5971, H5159, H5800): the LORD will not LEAVE His people, and His inheritance He will not abandon — 1 Samuel 12:22's promise, 'for his great name's sake', with verse 5's two possessives answered: the crushed people and the ground-down inheritance are still His. Paul builds Romans 11:1-2 on this line.

15.text: for judgment will come back around to righteousness, and all the upright in heart will follow after it.
15.amp: But judgment [mishpat] shall return [shub] unto righteousness [tsedek]: and all the upright [yashar] in heart [leb] shall follow ['shall be after it', achar, the KJV margin] it.
15.notes: ki-ad-tsedeq yashub mishpat (H6664, H7725, H4941): for judgment will RETURN to righteousness — the courts, now crooked (v. 20), will come back round to what they were for — ve-acharav kol-yishre-leb (H310, H3477, H3820): and after it, all the straight of heart — 'shall be after it', the margin's literal: following justice home like a procession. The promise inside the lament.

16.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? Who will take a stand for me against the workers of iniquity?
16.amp: Who will rise up [qum] for me against the evildoers [raa]? or who will stand up [yatsab — take a stand] for me against the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven]?
16.notes: mi-yaqum li im-mereim (H6965, H7489): who will RISE for me against the evildoers — mi-yityatseb li im-poale aven (H3320, H6466, H205): who will take a STAND for me against the workers of wickedness? The question expects the answer nobody — and then verse 17 gives it: the LORD, who was already there.

17.text: If the LORD had not been my help, my soul would soon have settled in silence.
17.amp: Unless [lule] the LORD [YHWH] had been my help, my soul [nephesh] had almost ['quickly', meat, the KJV margin] dwelt [shakan — settled] in silence.
17.notes: lule YHWH ezratah li (H3884, H3068): UNLESS the LORD were a help to me — Psalm 124:1's 'if not', in the singular — ki-meat shakhenah dumah naphshi (H4592, H7931, H5315): in a little — 'quickly', the margin — my soul would have SETTLED in dumah, silence, the grave's name in Psalm 115:17. The margin of survival was one Person wide.

18.text: When I said, 'My foot is slipping,' Your covenant love, O LORD, held me up.
18.amp: When I said [amar], My foot [regel] slips [mot — totters]; Your mercy [chesed — covenant love], O LORD [YHWH], held me up [saad — propped, sustained].
18.notes: im-amarti matah ragli (H559, H4131, H7272): when I said 'my foot has slipped' — the moment of Psalm 73:2 — chasdekha YHWH yisadeni (H2617, H3068, H5582): Your chesed, LORD, PROPPED me — saad, the bread-verb of Psalm 104:15 and the sickbed-verb of Psalm 41:3: covenant love as the hand under the arm. The most personal verse in a public psalm.

19.text: When cares swarm thick inside me, it is Your consolations that delight my soul.
19.amp: In the multitude [rob] of my thoughts [sarappim — anxious, branching thoughts] within [qereb] me Your comforts [tanchumim — consolations] delight [shaa] my soul [nephesh].
19.notes: be-rob sarappai be-qirbi (H7230, H8312, H7130): in the multitude of my sarappim — the disquieting, forking thoughts, a rare word from the root for branches — inside me; tanchumekha yeshaasheu naphshi (H8575, H8173, H5315): Your CONSOLATIONS make my soul play — shaa, the delight-verb of Psalm 119:16, a child's pleasure. Anxiety in the plural, comfort in the plural, and the second outnumbers the first (cf. 2 Corinthians 1:5).

20.text: Can a throne of destruction be allied with You — one that manufactures misery by statute?
20.amp: Shall the throne [kisse] of iniquity [havvah — ruin, destruction] have fellowship [chabar — be joined] with You, which frames [yatsar — forms] mischief [amal — trouble] by a law [choq — statute]?
20.notes: ha-yechobrekha kisse havvot (H2266, H3678, H1942): can a throne of havvot — ruinous cravings, calamities — be JOINED to You, chabar, the word for allies and for the tabernacle's coupled curtains; yotser amal ale-choq (H3335, H5999, H2706): that FORMS trouble by decree — injustice with a statute number. The psalm's sharpest political sentence: evil made legal is still evil, and God signs no treaty with it (cf. Isaiah 10:1).

21.text: They band together against the life of the righteous man and condemn innocent blood.
21.amp: They gather themselves together [gadad — troop up] against the soul [nephesh] of the righteous [tsaddiq], and condemn [rasha — pronounce guilty] the innocent [naqi] blood [dam].
21.notes: yagoddu al-nephesh tsaddiq (H1413, H5315, H6662): they TROOP against the life of the righteous — gadad, to band into a raiding party; ve-dam naqi yarshiu (H1818, H5355, H7561): and innocent blood they pronounce wicked — the court that convicts the victim, Naboth's court (1 Kings 21:13), and the Sanhedrin's (Matthew 27:24-25).

22.text: But the LORD has become my high stronghold, and my God the rock I run to.
22.amp: But the LORD [YHWH] is my defence [misgab — high stronghold]; and my God [Elohim] is the rock [tsur] of my refuge [machseh].
22.notes: va-yehi YHWH li le-misgab (H3068, H4869): and the LORD has BECOME to me a misgab, a high fortress — Psalm 9:9's word for the crushed man's refuge — v-Elohai le-tsur machsi (H430, H6697, H4268): and my God the rock of my machseh, my shelter. Against the throne of verse 20, a rock: the psalm sets two seats of power side by side and says which one it sits under.

23.text: He has turned their own iniquity back on them and will silence them in their own evil; the LORD our God will silence them.
23.amp: And He shall bring [shub — return] upon them their own iniquity [aven], and shall cut them off in their own wickedness [ra]; yea, the LORD [YHWH] our God [Elohim] shall cut them off.
23.notes: va-yasheb alehem et-onam (H7725, H205): and He has RETURNED on them their wickedness — verse 2's 'return recompense', granted; u-be-raatam yatsmitem (H7451): and in their own evil He will annihilate them — yatsmitem YHWH Elohenu (H3068, H430): the LORD our God will annihilate them, said twice. Psalm 7:16's boomerang as the last word: the wicked are not so much punished as allowed to complete themselves.
